angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 358,981 km at 22.45 pc = 0.21 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 44.5348 +/- 0.0267 mas (same row, RUWE 1.14): 22.45 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.516 +/- 0.016 solar radii from Lamontagne et al. 2026, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of GJ 3090 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026A&A...706A.278L/abstract): 358,981 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.519 +/- 0.013 solar masses from Lamontagne et al. 2026, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of GJ 3090 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026A&A...706A.278L/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3707 +/- 32 K from Lamontagne et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of GJ 3090 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026A&A...706A.278L/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Lamontagne et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of GJ 3090 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026A&A...706A.278L/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/gj-3090.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.728, rounded to two decimals
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of GJ 3090 (pscomppars): spectral type M2 V, from Lamontagne et al. 2026 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026A&A...706A.278L/abstract)
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of GJ 3090 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] 0.12 dex, from Lamontagne et al. 2026 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026A&A...706A.278L/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of GJ 3090 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -1.34199, from Lamontagne et al. 2026 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026A&A...706A.278L/abstract)
rotationPeriodSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of GJ 3090 (pscomppars): rotation period 17.95 d, from Lamontagne et al. 2026 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026A&A...706A.278L/abstract)
